Tables are lighter: one rule under the header, and row dividers only when a row wraps.

- A table used to draw a solid rule between every row, which doubled the height of a table of one-line rows and stacked three layers of chrome (box, header fill, rules). Now the box stays, the header is bold with a single rule under it, and rows of one line sit directly under each other. A three-row table is 7 lines tall, down from 9
- When any row wraps to several lines, rows are separated by a dotted rule so they stay apart. The solid rule is kept for the header alone, so the header reads as the header
- The header no longer has a gray fill. The fill was invisible in 256-color terminals (inside tmux) and looked patchy between cells; bold text reads the same everywhere
- The same look applies in replies, the Markdown preview pane, and the desk-asana and desk-slack panels. Narrow panes still switch a table to cards as before
- desk-plan and desk-review move to 0.80.4 with no changes

## Install

```
/plugin install desk-look --marketplace KyongSik-Yoon/cc-desktop-mod
```

Already installed: `/desk-update` (or `claude plugin update desk-look`), then `/reload-plugins`.
